finding: Duplicate world-graph placements for one objectId are all projected into the investigation bootstrap as SEPARATE WorldObjectDTOs with identical objectId.
probe: temp harness (Temp/opencode/phase6_adv) — API probes only, no product changes

repro.step1: Publish a CaseVersion whose draft.world_graph.placements contains TWO entries with the same object_id (e.g. apartment_lamp), e.g. anchors shelf_01/inspect (original) + kitchen_counter/read (injected).
repro.observed: bootstrap scene.worldObjects contains BOTH entries with objectId=apartment_lamp: [{anchor:shelf_01, interaction:inspect}, {anchor:kitchen_counter, interaction:read}].
repro.server_dispatch: POST .../objects/apartment_lamp/interact resolves placement_for_object sorting by (object_id, anchor): kitchen_counter wins (k<s). interact=read -> 200, interact=inspect -> 409 INTERACTION_NOT_ALLOWED.
repro.frontend_conflict: scene route model.worldObjects.find(objectId) picks the FIRST (shelf_01/inspect) and the client sends interaction=inspect, which the server answers 409 for the duplicated lamp -> the object appears interactable but every click errors.
repro.generation_guard_gap: backend/app/generation/safety.py validate_world_graph (lines 359-392) has NO uniqueness check across placements for object_id; backend/app/services/publication.py project_world_objects (lines 571-623) emits one DTO per placement with no per-objectId deduplication.

impact: Confusing/broken scene in the degenerate malformed-worldgraph case (Phase6 K); no truth leak; no state bypass (server dispatch stays deterministic). Reachable only via a published payload that violates placement uniqueness.
